claims.statement: The Crossref publication-trend record for PMT=IDS/IPS reports annual publication counts of 44 in 2021, 43 in 2022, 52 in 2023, and 58 in 2024, with an OLS slope of 5.1 works/year, a first-to-last delta of 14, total_results of 197, and a cutoff restricting records to those first deposited on or before 2024-12-31.

The Crossref publication-trend record explicitly states that it is an external publication-activity validation axis and does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness.

The supplied academic metadata records list three IDS/IPS-related Crossref publications: one titled Efficiency test of IDS/IPS systems against DOS and DDOS attacks; one titled THE BASIC MODES OF THE INTRUSION PREVENTION SYSTEM (IDS/IPS SURICATA) FOR THE COMPUTING CLUSTER, whose record content describes CPU utilization/load-average monitoring and optimization by hardware resources; and one titled Analisis Keamanan Jaringan Komputer Menggunakan Metode IDS dan IPS dengan Notifikasi Telegram, whose record content describes implementation/configuration and intrusion-scenario testing with Telegram notification.

The academic metadata records prohibit claims of deployment_maturity and operational_effectiveness, so their reported or described IDS/IPS topics cannot be used as proof of deployment readiness or operational effectiveness.

The MITRE ATT&CK mitigation record for M1029 includes an IDS/IPS log-forwarding measure, with an example of forwarding logs from IDS/IPS systems such as Zeek/Suricata to a remote security information system.

The MITRE ATT&CK record prohibits prevalence_magnitude and causal_effectiveness claims, so the IDS/IPS log-forwarding measure cannot be used to establish causal mitigation effectiveness or prevalence magnitude.

The CISA CPG records describe brute-force-relevant recommended controls: MFA prioritization for IT and OT accounts with remote access; alerting after consecutive unsuccessful login attempts and system-enforced login prevention for suspicious accounts; and unique credential provisioning to reduce credential reuse across IT and OT assets.

The NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 record discusses automatic system lockout or delay algorithms and alternative actions to help prevent brute force attacks, and notes that exceptions may be required based on operational mission or need.
The CISA CPG and NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 records prohibit exact_effectiveness and product_roi claims, so they do not quantify control effectiveness or financial return.

The threat-context records report brute-force-relevant observed context: DBIR reports 1,997 basic web application attack incidents and 881 with confirmed data disclosure and states threat actors continue to exploit default, simplistic, easily guessable credentials via brute forcing, buying, or reusing credentials; Mandiant M-Trends continues to observe password guessing against cloud sign-in portals to identify accounts without MFA configured; Mandiant's initial-infection-vector chart includes a 6% Brute Force value; and IBM X-Force reports vulnerabilities that make brute force attacks easier for attackers.

The allowed claim types for the cited threat-context records are limited to observed threat patterns, directional threat trends, observed attack vectors, or observed adversary behavior, and the cited threat-context records do not contain a financial metric, ROI, TCO, staffing cost, or budget impact.

conditional_requirements: A deployment-specific financial/adoption feasibility judgment would require supplied deployment context for budget_context, infrastructure_context, organization_type, and region.
A deployment-specific judgment would require evidence quantifying implementation cost, staffing/resource burden, integration effort, maintenance cost, and any benefit or cost avoidance.
Use of the positive publication trend must remain limited to publication activity and cannot be promoted to deployment readiness or financial justification.
Use of academic records must remain limited to reported publication topics and cannot be generalized to operational effectiveness or deployment maturity.
Use of control records must remain limited to recommended controls and cannot be used to infer exact control effectiveness or financial return.
constraints: The frozen deployment_context has null budget_context, infrastructure_context, organization_type, and region, so deployment-specific financial/adoption feasibility cannot be established.

Publication-activity evidence is bounded to publication activity and does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, causal mitigation effectiveness, cost, staffing, budget, or ROI.
Academic metadata records are bounded by prohibited claim types for deployment_maturity and operational_effectiveness.
Control records are bounded by prohibited claim types for exact_effectiveness and product_roi.
Threat-context records are bounded to observed threat context and do not provide financial benefit, cost avoidance, budget impact, or ROI.
evidence_gaps: No supplied record provides budget, procurement cost, total cost of ownership, licensing, vendor contracts, staffing hours, training cost, maintenance cost, or payback/ROI for IDS/IPS deployment.
No supplied record establishes organization-specific infrastructure capacity, integration effort, performance impact, or operational staffing burden for IDS/IPS deployment.
No supplied record distinguishes between general adoption feasibility and deployment-specific feasibility for the unknown organization_type, region, infrastructure_context, and budget_context.
No supplied record quantifies opportunity cost relative to alternative controls or implementation timing for the 2025-2027 window.
assessment.rationale: Under the financial/adoption lens, the supplied Stage 0 records provide limited general adoption signals for IDS/IPS: a positive publication-activity trend, academic metadata records describing IDS/IPS topics, and threat-context records showing brute-force-relevant attack behavior. These signals are bounded: publication activity does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, causal mitigation effectiveness, cost, staffing, budget, ROI, or deployment-specific feasibility. Control records describe relevant operational practices such as MFA prioritization, login-failure alerting/lockout, unique credential provisioning, and log forwarding, but they do not quantify financial or organizational burden. The frozen deployment context is null for budget_context, infrastructure_context, organization_type, and region, so a deployment-specific financial/adoption feasibility judgment cannot be made. Therefore, the records neither support nor materially challenge the frozen action's financial/adoption feasibility; the stance is indeterminate.
